card.name: Quadrille (Guadeloupean)
card.era: Introduced 18th c. (European colonists); creolized 19th c.; revived 1980s
card.tagline: Antillean Creole contredanse-derived figure dance with a caller.
card.profile: The kwadril (Creole quadrille) is a folk figure dance of the French Lesser Antilles derived from the European quadrille/contredanse, performed in Guadeloupe in sets of figures by four couples in a square, directed by a commandeur/konmande (caller) who announces the figures. Guadeloupean sets (balakadri/balkadri) combine proper quadrilles with creolized 19th-century couple dances - biguines, mazouks (mazurkas) and valses creoles. Instrumentation includes accordion, violin, guitar, tanbou dibas, chacha, malakach, triangle, tibwa and the syak (one-metre bamboo rasp). It was creolized by enslaved and freed Africans, who added African rhythms to the European ballroom forms (Wikipedia; CTIG).
card.insight: Antilleans regard the quadrille not as a colonial relic but as a 'new creation' adopted and transformed by people of African descent into a shared symbol of Creole identity across Guadeloupe, Martinique, Dominica and St. Lucia.
